name: Lithium brine; extraction and reinjection; at plant
description: This dataset represents lithium rich brine extraction from underground aquifer and reinjection of lithium lean brine into the aquifer. It is suitable for use with direct lithium extraction technologies (DLE), in which lithium is extracted from brine and lithium lean brine is returned to the aquifer. The functional unit of the process is the extraction and reinjection of 1 kg of lithium brine. The system boundary includes brine extraction and reinjection wells and associated pumps. In addition to electricity consumption, the resources extracted and emissions to water are included in the unit process as a difference between extraction and reinjection brine flows.
category: 21: Mining, Quarrying, and Oil and Gas Extraction/2123: Nonmetallic Mineral Mining and Quarrying

processDocumentation.timeDescription: This unit process is representative of lithium brine production in 2022. Data for electricity consumption comes from an industrial report published in 2022.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: This unit process is representative of lithium brine production in Canada. The brine concentrations are based on average Canadian values however, the process may be used in other regions in which the brine conentrations and technologies are similar.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: The technology used to extract lithium brine involves extracting lithium rich brine from underground aquifers and then reinjecting the lithium lean brine back into the underground aquifer. The direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology is described in the flow diagram below for Lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LiOH.H2O).
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Attributional and gate to gate process.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: This unit process for the extraction and reinjection of brine is based off a 20,000 metric ton of lithium hydroxide monohydrate production plant scale.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Technosphere flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. The mass balance for this process is not calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: The electricity consumption data for brine pumping and reinjection are based on a prospective direct lithium extraction (DLE) project in Canada. The amount of minerals extracted from environment are based on brine compostion measurement data.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Electricity consumption values were normalized based on amount of brine pumped out.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription:
Boundary Conditions: The system boundary includes brine extraction and reinjection wells and associated pumps. In addition to electricity consumption, the resources extracted and emissions to water are included in the unit process as a difference between extraction and reinjection brine flows. 
Data Collection: Data was extracted from an industry report and brine composition measurement data.
Uncertainty: Uncertainty was not evaluated for this process.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process was developed to be an input to lithium hydroxide monohydrate production. The direct lithium extraction (DLE) technology is described under the unit process for Lithium hydroxide monohydrate (LiOH.H2O).

reviews.details: Mass and energy balances were externally reviewed. LCA methodological aspects and comparison with literature were internally reviewed.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
SITUATION C1 -- ACCOUNTING The intended application for this process is for accounting purposes as described in Goal Situation C1 from the ILCD Handbook’s Detailed Guidance. LCA studies with this intended application offer "purely descriptive documentation of the system under analysis (e.g., a product, sector or country), without being interested in any potential consequences on other parts of the economy.” The studies categorized under Goal Situation C1 do consider existing benefits outside the analyzed system such as recycling.

The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system including existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model. The target audience of this model includes LCA practitioners, industry, and the general public.
